description: Each sector's methane emissions as a percentage of all methane emitted by the world or a country in a year, since 1990, as published by FAO, for the sectors that make up FAO's total: energy (fossil fuel production and use), industrial processes and product use, agriculture (livestock, rice, manure), land use (fires), waste and other, and, for the world only, international aviation and shipping. Where FAO publishes all six sectors, the shares add up to 100 (Tuvalu 2000, as printed, to 100.04). Food systems' methane runs across several of these sectors.

processing.description: Read Climate_change_Emissions_indicators_E_All_Data_(Normalized).csv from FAOSTAT's Emissions indicators (EM) bulk zip. The vintage is the domain's DateUpdate, 6 November 2026, from FAOSTAT's bulk-download catalogue (datasets_E.json), whose entry names this zip and gives FileRows 744,060, the number of data rows in this file. The zip was last modified on the server on Fri, 06 Nov 2026 16:55:13 GMT.

Kept the rows of element "Emissions Share (CH4)" (code 7265), unit "%", for the six IPCC sector items "Energy" (6821), "IPPU" (6817), "IPCC Agriculture" (1711), "LULUCF" (1707), "Waste" (6818), "Other" (6819), 1990–2024, as FAO prints them: each sector's methane as a percentage of the area's methane from all sectors (item "All sectors with LULUCF"). Nothing is computed here.
FAO prints a share for "International bunkers" (item 6820) where its total counts them (the World), published as a part of its own.

Checked that the shares add up to 100 within the rounding of values printed to 0.01 (0.005 a share) in each of the 1,513 area-years where FAO publishes all six sectors; the transform stops otherwise. Published as printed, although their shares add up to more than 100: TUV 2000 (100.0433). FAO divides each sector's methane by an all-sector total rounded to 0.0001 kilotonnes, which for a total this small moves the shares by more than their own rounding.

FAO publishes no row for some parts of some areas' methane splits. Those parts are left missing, never filled or set to zero, and a sector without a share is one for which FAOSTAT's emissions totals (GT) have no methane row for that area and year, so it is not part of the whole. scope.basis: FAO's published shares (FAOSTAT Emissions indicators, element "Emissions Share (CH4)") of methane by mass, so no global warming potential is involved. The whole is FAO's all-sector methane ("All sectors with LULUCF"). FAOSTAT's six IPCC sectors: energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture, land use, land-use change and forestry (for methane, fires in forests and in organic (peat) soils; forests take up carbon dioxide, not methane, so nothing is subtracted and the share is never below zero), waste and other. International aviation and shipping (bunker fuels) are counted in the World's total only, as a part of their own, since FAO's release of 6 November 2026; no country's total includes them. Agriculture and land use are FAO's own Tier 1 estimates; energy, industry, waste and other are PRIMAP-hist v2.8 third-party estimates, which count some territories inside their parent country (for example Bermuda in the United Kingdom, Greenland and the Faroe Islands in Denmark, Palestine in Israel, Puerto Rico in the United States). So such a parent country's energy, industry, waste and other emissions include those territories while its agriculture and land use do not, and for 27 territories in the November 2026 release FAO has no energy, industry, waste or other rows, so their total covers agriculture and land use only. Estimates, not country inventory submissions.
scope.geography: The world, countries and territories, and the European Union (27)
